data.name: Khushhaal
data.gender_notes: Khushhaal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘khushu’, meaning ‘to be sincere’ or ‘to be loyal to Allah’. In Islamic tradition, it is a name given to those who strive for righteousness and remain steadfast in their faith. The name evokes images of deep spiritual commitment, peaceful devotion, and unwavering loyalty. The name Khushhaal carries the meaning “Loyal, faithful, sincere” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khushhaal usually hope their child will grow to embody loyal, faithful, sincere and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the sincere bond between the servant and Allah.
data.etymology: Khushhaal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Loyal, faithful, sincere.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khushhaal total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 12, page 242 The name Khushhaal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Khushhaal was a Persian prince who ruled Khorasan (a region in present-day Iran) during the early Abbasid era. He is famous for his valour and generosity, and was a patron of scholars and poets. He was a contemporary of Harun al-Rashid and Caliph Ma'mon, and his death is believed to have occurred around 820 CE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Aghanis Al-Siqah Al-Nafisah, Volume 1, page 210 The name Khushhaal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Khushhaal was also mentioned in the epic poem Aghanis by Ferdowsi, as the brave and just ruler of the city of Balkh (present-day Afghanistan). He is described as a model of chivalry and loyalty, who was loved by his people and respected by his enemies.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Khushhaal remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
